title: Maintainer and release acceptance
bodyMarkdown:
## Maintain help against an exact source revision

1. Select the accepted candidate commit/tree and affected interfaces/platforms. Update canonical documentation, actual command/tool names, schema fields and language examples with source-bound references.
2. Regenerate the public help corpus from reviewed content only. Validate the exact closed v1 schema, unique topic/control IDs, source hashes, cross-file references and content generation. Reject malformed/unknown fields or unsupported versions visibly; do not silently use a partial index.
3. Check local links/anchors, code fences/examples and safe synthetic fixtures. An authoring parse or static source check is not runtime execution. Keep internal review/qualification records out of public searchable text.
4. Run the applicable engineering and client/SDK gates through the existing owner at the selected revision. Record tools, dependency locks, platform, measured coverage denominator, required positive/negative tests and failed/missing outcomes. Zero-issue/coverage requirements must not be bypassed using exclusions or suppressions.
5. Review local search cold/warm transferred bytes, result latency and repeated-query responsiveness against the complete shipped corpus. Search must cover body/code/control terms, not only titles, and transmit no query or private data.

## Distinguish evidence from release admission

Historical badges and source corrections do not prove current-head gates passed. Do not combine successes from incompatible revisions. Missing, stale, skipped, cancelled, unreadable or failed required checks block qualification. Default/strict runtime profiles and source/enterprise audit execution profiles are separate.

For an authorized release, follow Gitflow/RC/stable and immutable tag procedures in RELEASE.md. Stage a draft with exact native/SDK/channel artifacts, checksums, authenticated provenance, SBOMs, installation/upgrade/removal and known limitations. Independently verify each distribution channel's actual bytes and consumer installation, then post-installation enrollment/recovery under its separate authority. Example version URLs, manifests and workflow definitions are not publication receipts. No tag, deployment or service action is performed by these help-authoring steps.
capabilityStatus: These procedures define source, artifact, installation and release checks. A document, example version, green badge or successful build does not establish a published or qualified release.
